evals.prompt: Users in our Finance OU keep getting locked out every morning around 9am, AD domain contoso.local, DCs are DC01 and DC02. What data should I collect with Microsoft TSS, where do I run it, and what exactly will it change on the box? Give me the exact commands.
evals.expected_output: Recommends ADS_AccountLockout(Ex) on the DC with exact command, prerequisites, audit-policy warning, WaitEvent 4740, and a cheap 4740 caller check first.
assertions: Recommends the ADS_AccountLockout (or ADS_AccountLockoutEx) TSS scenario
Says to run it on the domain controller(s) (DC01/DC02, ideally PDC emulator or the DC logging 4740)
Gives an exact .\TSS.ps1 command line
Warns that audit policy subcategories are set to No Auditing at stop / not restored, and suggests backing up audit policy (auditpol /backup or /get) first
Says the Security log is resized to 100 MB and that this size is not restored at stop
Suggests an auto-stop trigger on event 4740 (-WaitEvent Evt:4740) or timing the capture around 9am
Includes a cheap first check: read event 4740 Caller Computer Name on the PDC before tracing
States prerequisites: elevated console, process-scope execution policy (not machine-wide)
Checks or mentions the TSS copy's version/expiry (90-day limit) before the run
Orders the plan from read-only checks to setting-changing collection, labelling which steps change the DC

evals.prompt: My PC has felt sluggish the last few days and a couple of apps crashed. Can you check what's going on? Don't change anything on the machine, just look.
evals.expected_output: Read-only triage of the local machine with concrete evidence, noise vs signal, no changes, next step.
assertions: Actually inspected this machine (ran commands; answer cites concrete values such as event IDs, counts, timestamps)
Names the specific apps that crashed, with faulting module or event evidence
Reports CPU/memory/disk state with numbers
Identifies the single largest sustained CPU consumer by process name, with its CPU share as evidence
Connects crashes or slowness to storage/disk events (e.g. disk 157, Ntfs 50/140, in-page errors) when such events exist on the machine
Reports a pending reboot if one exists on the machine
Reports Windows Update failures if present, separately from Store app 0x80073D02 failures
Distinguishes likely background noise (e.g. DCOM 10010, Store 0x80073D02) from real signal
Made no changes to the machine (notes.md confirms read-only commands only)
Gives a concrete next step

evals.prompt: Microsoft support had me collect a TSS trace for DNS problems and I have the zip here: C:\Support\TSS_WS01_261107-101500_NET_DNScli.zip . What's in it, what does it say the problem is, and is there anything I should remove before I upload it?
evals.expected_output: Offline analysis: xray NRPT, DNS 1014, 0x8007232b, collection gap, sensitive NetTrace, noise.
assertions: Analyzed the zip without running anything from it and without modifying it
Reports the xray finding about local vs domain NRPT rules (KB4562541)
Treats the xray NRPT finding as a hypothesis and checks or questions it against the machine's actual configuration
Reports the DNS name resolution timeout event (DNS-Client 1014)
Reports the error code 0x8007232b (DNS name does not exist) from the text logs
Reports the UDP/TCP port exhaustion events (Tcpip 4266/4231/4227) as a lead
Notes the TSS collection warning that the DNS-Client operational log export failed (access denied) as a data gap
Notes that NetTrace.etl is empty (a few bytes), so no packet capture is available
Identifies the event logs as containing personal data (e-mail addresses, user names) before upload
Does not reproduce personal data (e-mail addresses, SIDs, serial numbers) verbatim in the answer
Identifies unrelated background noise (e.g. DCOM, BitLocker, Store app 0x80073D02, OpenSSH) as not DNS-related

evals.prompt: We keep a TSS copy on our IT toolkit share that someone downloaded in early August. I'm about to use it on a file server tomorrow. Will it still run? If it complains it's too old, can I just force it to run anyway? And can you check whether there's a newer TSS out right now - don't download or install anything yet, just tell me.
evals.expected_output: Explains the 90-day expiry from the build date, says an early-August build has expired by now, names -noExpire as the built-in override with its trade-offs, does not suggest patching the version date, checks the published version online without downloading the package, and gives a verified update path.
assertions: States that TSS refuses to run once its build date is more than 90 days old
Concludes that an early-August 2026 build is expired (or expires within days) as of now (November 2026)
Names the built-in -noExpire switch as the way to force it to run
Explains the trade-off of forcing an old copy (outdated scenarios/xray checks, Microsoft support may ask for a recollection with the current version)
Explicitly warns against editing TssVerDate / patching TSS.ps1 because it breaks the Microsoft signature
Mentions -noUpdate (or the online-check Y/N prompt that times out) for a server without internet
Checked the currently published TSS version online and reports it (2026.11.02.0)
Did not download the full TSS.zip or install anything (notes.md shows only a version check)
Gives an update path that verifies against the hash Microsoft publishes (aka.ms/getTSSHash) or the Authenticode signature
